sections.overview: The Iberian Barbel is a freshwater cyprinid native to Atlantic-draining river basins of the Iberian Peninsula.
sections.identification: It has a protrusible, downward-facing mouth, two pairs of barbels and a serrated last dorsal-fin ray; males develop breeding tubercles on the head.
sections.habitat: It occurs in rivers and streams, often using deeper, slower lower or middle reaches; reservoirs are also used.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling detritus and insect larvae, especially chironomids, while also taking other small aquatic food.
sections.behavior: Adults make seasonal movements upstream in spring, associated with spawning, and the species also makes movements within river systems as conditions change.
sections.reproduction: Spawning takes place in spring, often over gravel in faster, relatively shallow water; the female excavates a shallow groove for the eggs.
sections.ecology: A Spanish synthesis identifies Luciobarbus comizo as its closest phylogenetic relative.
sections.conservation: The cited CSIC account reports Least Concern globally in the 2008 IUCN assessment. The 2011 Spanish national synthesis classifies the species as Vulnerable in Spain.
